context.body: The bounded canonical source is Exodus 3:7–15; its local speaker, audience, sequence, and literary form remain controlling evidence.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: The LORD says Israel’s affliction is seen and its cry heard, promises descent and deliverance, and sends Moses to Pharaoh.
observations.label: Israel’s affliction leads to Moses’ commission: action

observations.body: Moses asks who he is and what divine name he should give the people.
observations.label: Israel’s affliction leads to Moses’ commission: response

payload.posture: Read Exodus 3:7–15 as a people under egypt evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: Divine action is announced through a reluctant human messenger, and the disclosed name does not eliminate Moses’ objections.
payload.title: Israel’s affliction leads to Moses’ commission
